governed_construct: Every typed position in the unit: each function/method/arrow parameter, each variable/property/class-member declaration, each function return, each type annotation and each type assertion. One instance is one such position; its verdict is decided by the type the TypeScript checker assigns to it.
interpretation: The rule asks that every value's type be statically known and never `any`. An instance is VIOLATED if its type is `any`, whether written explicitly (`: any`, `any[]`, `Promise<any>`, `as any`) or obtained implicitly: a parameter with no annotation and no contextual type (implicit any, including untyped JavaScript parameters), or a declaration whose inferred type is `any` (e.g. `const x = JSON.parse(s)`). An instance conforms if it is explicitly annotated with a non-any type, or if its type is a non-any type supplied by inference that the checker resolves (a contextually typed callback parameter such as `orders.map((order) => ...)` over a typed array, or a variable initialised from a typed expression). `unknown` is a conforming explicit type. Omitted return-type annotations are not by themselves violations; positive fixtures annotate them anyway. Mentions of `any` in comments or strings are not instances. A unit with no declarations, parameters, annotations or assertions (only statements such as top-level calls with literal arguments) is NOT_APPLICABLE.
